population.note: FICTIONAL. Adults ≈274M. Current 36.2% ≈ 99.2M. Ever 48.5% ≈ 132.9M, up 13.0 pts, inside the 14.2 limit. Used-and-off-now 12.3 pts ≈ 33.7M. Never-used ≈ 141M. Cycling: ≈17.0 pts of current users are on a second or later course, and ≈5.0 pts of the off-now group restarted and stopped again, so (17.0+5.0)/48.5 ≈ 45%. This is unchanged from 2032. The 50 mg pill raised one-year persistence among new oral starters to ~45%, but the larger long-term 65+ population added more bone pauses, and the two roughly cancel. Age check: 18–29 22% × 52M = 11.4M; 30–49 42% × 91M = 38.2M; 50–64 52% × 62M = 32.2M; 65+ 25% × 69M = 17.3M; total ≈ 99.2M. The under-30 jump from 13.5% to 22% is not about weight. It comes from the needle-free 50 mg pill, AUD prescribing after the 2033 guideline (≈1.6M users across all ages, ~40% under 35), 'calm' and 'focus' subscriptions (6.0M, up from 3.5M), and gray-market oral copies. The 65+ band rose only from 17% to 25% even though the Part D benefit is permanent. Roughly one in four 65+ ever-users is now off on a medically advised bone pause or a DEXA-wait lapse. Income: the bottom third, at 33.5%, includes ≈6M of the ≈9.7M gray-market users and is under-measured. The never-used population (~141M) is now a minority of under-50 adults in high-uptake suburbs. It is concentrated among rural residents of the 19 non-adopting states, people with contraindications, refusers by conviction, and a new urban under-30 cohort who describe abstention as an aesthetic. Pediatric: 1.5% of ~73M ≈ 1.1M, of whom ≈150k are under 12, mostly ages 6–11 after the May 2034 semaglutide approval, under specialist care with growth and bone monitoring. About one child in two now lives with a parent who is on the drug or cycling off it.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. Status quo structure. The permanent Part D obesity benefit (BMI ≥30, or ≥27 with a comorbidity) continues with a $50 copay and the counselling visit. Under the Aug 2033 HHS deal the negotiated rate fell from $199 to $175 from Jan 2034. Medicare pays 17.6% of fills ≈ 17.5M users: ≈6.6M diabetes, ≈10.2M obesity, ≈0.7M AUD under compendia listing. Obesity benefit 2034: 10.2M × $175 × 12 ≈ $21.4B gross; beneficiaries pay 10.2M × $50 × 12 ≈ $6.1B; the program pays ≈$15.3B, above the ≈$14B/yr CBO average because volume outran the price cut. All Medicare incretin fills: 17.5M × $175 × 12 ≈ $36.8B gross. Medicaid: the same 31 states plus DC on the 90% match and continuation standard, with no adopters added or lost. Medicaid pays 14.1% of fills ≈ 14.0M users × $175 × 12 ≈ $29.4B gross before supplemental rebates. AUD use is now covered as a medically accepted indication in every Medicaid program, including the 19 non-adopting states, which pay it at regular FMAP. That is the main way the non-adopting states' poor reach the drug legally.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 100+ semaglutide brands at $4–25/month, plus generic oral semaglutide including 50 mg, and orforglipron copies sold domestically ahead of patent resolution. China: generic semaglutide and tirzepatide, and research-grade retatrutide API that feeds the gray trade. Canada: generic semaglutide at CAD 45–70. Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and Egypt have generics. In the US the 2033 settlement entry date passed with no launch. FDA complete-response letters (Mar 2033) on synthetic-peptide impurity, immunogenicity and pen-device equivalence push first approval to 2035 at the earliest.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Managed decline. Generic semaglutide missed its 2033 date, and HHS and the manufacturers agreed a step-down in Aug 2033. Portal prices: injectable semaglutide and tirzepatide $179–249; starting-dose orals $139; Wegovy pill 50 mg $249 portal; retatrutide $349 direct ($1,499 list); amycretin $399; MariTide $449 a month. List prices are mostly unchanged and Wegovy is still $1,349. PBM net under outcomes contracts ≈$155–170. Payer mix of ≈99.2M users: commercial 36.3% (36.0M), Medicare 17.6% (17.5M), Medicaid 14.1% (14.0M), cash/direct 22.2% (22.0M, including ≈6.0M 'calm' and 'focus' subscribers), imported, counterfeit or gray-compounded 9.8% (9.7M). Sum 99.2M = 100%. The gray share rose because of the missed generic date, cheap small-molecule oral copies, and offshore telehealth storefronts selling 'research' retatrutide. ≈75% of covering employers still gate, with no pause exemption. The 503B exclusion and 503A injunction stand on paper, and med-spa 'peptide clinics' operate around them.

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. The oral_parity driver is met by an existing product in a new form. No novel oral candidate in the starting pipeline was past phase 2. In Jun 2033 FDA approved a 50 mg maintenance dose of the Wegovy pill on 72-week head-to-head data showing non-inferiority to injectable semaglutide 2.4 mg (≈17% versus ≈16% mean loss). It matches the mainstream injectable but not tirzepatide or retatrutide, so the needle barrier is gone for most users while top-efficacy regimens remain injected. Survodutide (PDUFA early 2033) was approved Feb 2033. MariTide was approved Oct 2033 after its 72-week DEXA data, and as a monthly injectable it is the first product to make the 'monthly' route real. Bimagrumab combinations: phase 3 completed and BLA filed Jan 2034, decision no earlier than 2035, and still the most watched lean-mass-sparing agent. Oral amycretin is in phase 3 and not filed. Pediatric under-12 approvals are supplemental labels on existing molecules. US incretin market 2034 ≈ $185B: ≈89.5M paying users × ≈$172 average net × 12. Ex-US ≈ $24B and eroding.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the most common effect and the leading cause of voluntary stops. Slightly lower on the slow-titrated 50 mg pill and higher during retatrutide and survodutide escalation.
Absolute numbers keep rising with ~99M users and more high-loss regimens.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low. Gray-market product increasingly confounds reports.
A population problem. A 2034 Medicare claims update estimates ≈2.1M long-term older users meet sarcopenia criteria, up from 1.3M. In untrained users over 50, lean mass is ~30–40% of weight lost.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class label retained. Body-composition monitoring is in the 12 mg retatrutide, amycretin and MariTide labels. The CMS continuation standard requires annual DEXA for long-term 65+ users. MA strength benefits are now near-universal.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Third wave year. ≈8.5M users aged 65+ have more than 2 years' use. 8.5M × 0.6%/yr × 0.35 ≈ 18,000 excess hip fractures a year against ~305,000 US total, plus an estimated 8–12k excess vertebral fractures among cycling postmenopausal women 50–64. Medicare DEXA claims are up ~200% since 2028, and waits run 16–24 weeks across the Sun Belt and Midwest.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelling retained; bone endpoints required in all filings. The CMS 'bone pause' code (90 days) is unchanged, and private gated plans are still not bound by it. The DOJ civil case against Novo is unresolved.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohorts still conflict; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label; FDA warnings mention; no class determination.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association, including in AUD-indication cohorts.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia, 'the grey')
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Retatrutide 12 mg: ~12% versus ~5% of comparators cross a SHAPS threshold, observational and dose-dependent. A first independent cohort of low-dose 'calm' subscribers (academic, n≈4,000, 2034) finds ~7% versus ~5% on a matched comparison, which is not statistically clear. The AUD guideline itself cites reward modulation as the presumed mechanism.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FTC consent orders bar 'anxiety treatment' claims; 'calm' and 'focus' permitted. No label change. FDA asked for SHAPS in the AUD sNDA.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Millions of regain episodes a year from gating drop-offs, bone pauses and DEXA-wait lapses.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The CMS bone-pause code softens it for Medicare. The Seventh Circuit has not ruled on the Indiana waiver.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Iron, B12, vitamin D, calcium and protein insufficiency are common in high-loss older users. There is a new concern in 6–11-year-olds on treatment, who have less margin.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance; Part D counselling screen. Pediatric labels require dietitian involvement.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~8 years; adolescent exposure; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About twelve years of follow-up. The adolescent bone-accrual question is unresolved: an expanded interim readout in 2034 still shows lower BMD gain in rapid losers, and the effect is not yet characterised as permanent. Cycling still looks worse for bone than continuous use.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Full adolescent data due 2034 were extended to 2035 at sponsor request. Postmarketing requirements continue.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported / gray-market product harms
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Rising again. Poison-centre GLP-1 calls are up ~40% from 2032. Gray-market orforglipron-copy capsules show 0–180% of label content in FDA sampling. 'Research' retatrutide vials cause dosing errors, injection-site infections and some 12 mg-equivalent overdoses in first-time users. There is a small cluster of liver-enzyme elevations linked to an impurity in one Chinese API lot.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alert expanded to small-molecule GLP-1 API. FDA–DEA warning letters to offshore telehealth storefronts (Sep 2034). Individuals still not prosecuted. 'Safe Pens' bill still stalled.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent, higher at 12 mg; usually transient.

safety_ledger.effect: Falls and frailty-related injury in older users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Fall-related ED visits remain elevated in 65+ users with more than 2 years' use. The absolute count is rising with the larger long-term cohort.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Fall-risk screening is mandatory in the Part D counselling visit.

safety_ledger.effect: Adverse body-composition cycling (fat-dominant regain after lean-dominant loss)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Upgraded. Multiple DEXA cohorts confirm that repeated cycles leave users at the same weight with less lean mass and more visceral fat, worst in people over 50 who were cut off by gating or DEXA-wait lapses.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: In the 2034 joint guidance as a reason to avoid unplanned stops. No regulatory action on private gating.

safety_ledger.effect: Heart-rate elevation at high triple-agonist doses
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A mean resting heart-rate rise of several bpm at 12 mg retatrutide and a smaller rise on survodutide; arrhythmia significance unclear.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled precaution; cardiovascular outcomes trial ongoing.

safety_ledger.effect: Pediatric (6–11) growth velocity and bone-age effects
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New entry. In the pivotal under-12 trials a minority of children showed slowed height velocity during rapid loss. Long-term data are absent. ≈150k children under 12 are on treatment.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Label requires growth charting every 3 months and bone-age assessment at baseline; pediatric postmarketing registry required.

food_and_beverage.state: With 36% of adults on the drug, US salty-snack volume falls ~5% a year and confectionery ~6%. A third major packaged-food group spun off its snack division in 2033. Protein, fortified dairy and 'bone-forward' lines lead growth, and a premium 'fed' segment has appeared: full-fat, butter-heavy and marbled meat marketed to young urban buyers as appetite pride. Grocers keep 'on-plan' aisles and add 'lift' aisles.

alcohol.state: Seventh straight year of US spirits volume decline, now ~25% below 2027. AUD guideline prescribing removed a slice of the heaviest-drinking decile, which is disproportionately valuable to spirits makers. Beer is down. Non-alcoholic formats are growing. Tobacco and vape are falling faster than trend.

restaurants.state: Traffic is roughly flat. Spend per cover is down ~12% from 2028 in high-uptake suburbs. Half portions are standard. At the same time Brooklyn, Austin and Los Angeles have 'appetite rooms': long tasting menus and steakhouse revivals where under-30s eat big in public as a status display. Heritage 'full table' rooms in Atlanta, Memphis and Houston endure.

apparel.state: The aesthetic inversion moved demand. Slim fits are discounted, and cuts sized for muscle in the shoulder and thigh sell out among urban under-30s. Cycling-sized rental keeps growing. The plus segment has shrunk but is stable at specialists.

fitness.state: Growing fastest of any adjacent sector. 'Built' is the scarce body, and muscle takes time, coaching and DEXA. DEXA-plus-coaching chains doubled their sites. Medicare Advantage 'prescribed lifting' is near-universal. Staff qualified to train older and pediatric lifters remain the constraint.

insurance.state: Employer coverage is 68%, still ~75% gated. Pharmacy trend is ~+5% as volume growth outpaces a ~10% net price fall. Fracture, fall and rehab costs are visible in Medicare Part A and Medicare Advantage bids. Life insurers ask why BMI ≥30 applicants are untreated. Two carriers now ask about DEXA history.

pharma.state: Volume up ~45% while net price is down ~10%. Lilly leads on retatrutide, tirzepatide and Foundayo. Novo regained momentum with the 50 mg pill and AUD guideline listing, and the generic delay was a windfall for it. Amgen entered with MariTide and Boehringer with survodutide. Bone-agent and DEXA makers keep winning. Indian and Chinese makers sell openly abroad and through gray channels into the US.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Thin is no longer information. A $25 Hyderabad pen, a $139 pill or a Medicaid kiosk plan can produce it, so it stopped signalling discipline or money. What signals now is what the drug cannot cheaply make: visible muscle, bone density spoken of like a credit score, and an appetite displayed in public. Among urban under-30s in Brooklyn, Austin and LA, 'unmedicated' or 'low-dose and lifting' is the prestige look. Visible regain is still read as a lost plan, and the thin-armed stoop is still read as an old, under-coached user.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The class line moved from thin versus fat to built versus merely thin. Top-third users run low-maintenance or 50 mg pill regimens with coaching, scheduled DEXA, antiresorptives and $300/month in protein and training. Bottom-third users reach thinness through Medicaid continuation plans, AUD-listed prescriptions or gray pens, often without a scan. They now find that the look they paid for reads as cheap. In Dayton and Tulsa, the mobile DEXA van is still where retirees gather. In Austin, a DEXA printout is a dating-app photo.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Protein-first meals remain the suburban default, with hosts planning for 'on' guests. In parallel, urban 'fed' supper clubs and appetite rooms make eating a lot a performance, and some of the diners are on low doses and eat on dose-holiday weekends. Church potlucks and heritage full-table dinners persist. Parents of newly treated 6–11-year-olds argue at school about birthday cake.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps keep the on/off/pausing field and now add 'lifting' and 'DEXA verified' badges. 'Unmedicated' has moved from a niche filter to an aspirational one among urban under-30s, and a small scandal of people faking it has followed. Advice columns field complaints about partners whose 'calm' subscription has flattened the relationship, and about partners who refuse to start.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Two meanings run side by side. In clinics and suburbs, appetite is a managed variable. Among the young urban affluent, it is a recovered luxury and proof of vitality. The 2030 backlash coalition (Atlanta body-sovereignty collectives, Tulsa–Dallas 'appetite is a gift' congregations, disability advocates) gained unexpected cultural allies in the inversion, but not political ones. Most inversion adherents are not against the drug, only against looking like they need it.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Top-dose retatrutide: ~12% versus ~5% cross a SHAPS threshold, observational and dose-dependent. With ~8–9M Americans on top-dose triple or dual regimens, that implies on the order of 550–650k excess cases of clinically meaningful anhedonia if causal. The first independent 'calm' subscriber cohort (2034) finds ~7% versus ~5%, which is not clearly distinguishable from zero. ≈6.0M subscribers sit inside the ≈22.0M cash/direct users. The AUD guideline names reward modulation as the presumed therapeutic mechanism, which gives the same effect a clinical endorsement.
interior_life.framing: Feature in retail, treatment in addiction medicine, side effect in obesity clinics. 'Quiet', 'Even' and 'Unhooked' now cost $129–169 a month after the step-down, and 'craving freedom' copy borrows the AUD guideline's language without naming it. Users still call the bad version 'the grey'. A growing young subculture calls the unblunted state 'colour'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: 'Focus' subscriptions are standard in large-employer lifestyle accounts. Two staffing firms in call centres and logistics bundle them into onboarding wellness kits. EAPs now route problem drinkers to AUD prescribing as the default first referral. In sales, hospitality and creative work, people still dose down before pitches and service peaks. Unions bargain over gated-plan data and copy the CMS bone-pause exemption into contracts.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: The 'grey era' of mid-tempo pop is a critical cliché. The aesthetic inversion produced a counter-scene: 'colour' nights, loud venues, competitive eating dinners, hot-sauce festivals, and Nashville and Austin acts that market themselves as unmedicated, some of them truthfully. Escape rooms, extreme sports and ultra-spicy food keep growing among users who want stronger stimulus.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists screen for dose, subscriptions and AUD prescriptions. Dose-holiday weekends are routine, and 'restart' anti-nausea packs sit by the pharmacy register. Couples counselling increasingly involves one partner on 'Quiet' and the other pursuing 'colour'. Parents of treated 9-year-olds ask pediatricians whether their child seems less excited by things.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The 2034 midterms are fought over who pays and the missed generic date, which both parties call a betrayal and blame on each other. DEXA capacity is a senior-lobby issue in Arizona and Florida races. The continuation standard remains contested but unchanged. No new state action. 'Calm voter' turnout effects are still unpublished speculation, and inversion-aligned young voters do not form a bloc.

state.regulatory_posture: FDA remains data-demanding. It rejected the first generic semaglutide applications on synthetic-peptide and device grounds, approved the 50 mg pill and two new injectables with DEXA requirements, and approved under-12 labels with growth monitoring. FDA–DEA warning letters and import alerts target offshore storefronts but cannot keep up. FTC enforcement is claims-based only.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Status quo. Permanent Part D obesity benefit with a $50 copay, now at a $175 rate. 90% Medicaid match in the same 31 states plus DC. AUD coverage flows through existing medically-accepted-indication rules. No individual mandate.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: The CMS continuation standard is unchanged: ≥80% PDC, a verified weigh-in every 6 months, ≥5% loss at 6 months or a clinician override, annual DEXA for long-term 65+ users, and a 90-day bone-pause code. DEXA waits of 16–24 weeks mean a growing number of seniors run up against the annual scan requirement. CMS lets clinicians attest 'scan ordered' as an interim but has not changed the rule. Private gating covers ~75% of employer plans. Indiana and Arkansas 12-month rules continue. BMI-linked wellness surcharges up to 30% continue.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT sleep-apnea screening still pushes drivers to tirzepatide, and fleets require DEXA for drivers over 55. The VA adopted the AUD guideline and is among the largest AUD prescribers. Army accession policy is still contested; the Air Force waiver stands.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Chinese API, now including small-molecule GLP-1 API that is easy to synthesise, and Indian finished product supply both the legal world market and the US gray market. The US–India 'pharmaceutical parcel cooperation' language is unchanged and import is not legalised. Section 232 tariffs remain. Lilly's 12 mg allocation eased in 2033 after Irish fill-finish expansion.

events.event: FDA approves a 50 mg maintenance dose of the Wegovy pill after a head-to-head trial shows it is as effective as the weekly injection at about 17% average loss; within a year more new starts are on pills than on pens

Five months after FDA rejected the first generic semaglutide applications over peptide impurities and pen design, HHS and manufacturers agree a price step-down: portal injectables to $179–249, starting pills to $139, and the Medicare and Medicaid rate from $199 to $175 in January 2034, with the $50 copay unchanged

Addiction psychiatrists' joint guideline endorses semaglutide as a second-line treatment for alcohol use disorder; compendia listing follows, Medicaid programmes in all states begin covering it, and the VA adopts it

Updated Medicare claims analysis puts excess hip fractures among long-term older users at about 18,000 a year and finds DEXA waits of 16–24 weeks; CMS lets doctors attest a scan is 'ordered' but declines to change the annual-scan rule

FDA approves weekly semaglutide for obese children aged 6 to 11, with growth charting every three months and a mandatory registry, after a trial in which some children's height growth slowed during rapid loss

FDA and DEA warning letters to 40 offshore telehealth storefronts selling 'research' retatrutide vials and copied orforglipron capsules; agency sampling finds capsule doses ranging from zero to nearly double the label

open_tensions: Generic semaglutide missed its 2033 date on FDA's peptide and device objections. The public bill is still priced at a negotiated $175 rather than a generic price, while ≈9.7M Americans buy $4–40 product, including copied small-molecule pills that are trivially easy to make. When generics do land in 2035, they will reprice everything at once.

The annual DEXA requirement and the 16–24-week wait are on a collision course. About 18,000 excess hip fractures a year are billed to Part A while the drug is billed to Part D, and private gated plans still have no bone-pause exemption. A 58-year-old who follows bone guidance can lose the coverage her mother keeps.

The AUD guideline gave reward modulation a clinical blessing just as ≈6.0M non-obese people buy it as 'calm' and 'focus' from employer catalogues. Meanwhile the best data show dose-dependent anhedonia at top doses, and the line between treatment, product and harm is now drawn only by marketing copy.

Thinness became cheap and lost its prestige just as the poorest third reached it. The new status body requires muscle, coaching and scans the bottom third cannot buy. ≈150k children under 12 have started treatment with growth-velocity questions open and adolescent bone data delayed to 2035.
still_true: Wegovy's list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.

The CMS continuation standard's terms are unchanged: ≥80% PDC, a verified weigh-in every 6 months, ≥5% loss at 6 months or a clinician override, annual DEXA for long-term 65+ users, and the 90-day 'bone pause' code.
Exactly 31 states plus DC have adopted the Medicaid continuation standard for the 90% federal match; none added, none withdrew.
The Indiana and Arkansas Medicaid 1115 waivers still end coverage for 12 months after two missed verifications, and the Seventh Circuit has still not ruled.
The 503B exclusion and the 503A injunction against compounded semaglutide and tirzepatide still stand.

prose.headline: Thin Is Cheap Now: In 2034, the body that costs money is fed, built, scanned and, if you can prove it, unmedicated
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2034 a little more than one American adult in three is on an incretin drug. The share stopped being news long ago, and the more interesting fact is how many of them are swallowing it. In June 2033 the FDA approved a fifty-milligram maintenance dose of the Wegovy pill after a trial showed it worked as well as the weekly injection. Within a year more people were starting on pills than on pens. The strongest regimens, Lilly's twelve-milligram triple agonist and the new monthly shots from Amgen, are still injected. For the ordinary user, though, the needle is gone, and the twenty-somethings who never wanted one are now in the numbers.

The generic that was supposed to change the economics did not arrive. Semaglutide's settled 2033 entry date passed without a launch, because the FDA rejected the first applications over peptide impurities and the pen device. The government accepted a managed step-down instead: portal injectables at $179 to $249, starting pills at $139, and the Medicare and Medicaid rate cut from $199 to $175 in January. The payers are the same as before. Medicare is still the largest buyer, the same thirty-one states and Washington, D.C. take the ninety-percent match, and three-quarters of employer plans still gate. Nearly ten million Americans buy outside all of it. They use Indian pens, Chinese vials labelled for research, and copied capsules of Lilly's small-molecule pill. That last product is easy to synthesise, and when the FDA sampled it this autumn the doses ranged from nothing to nearly twice the label.

The drug picked up two indications that change who uses it. In November 2033 the addiction psychiatrists endorsed semaglutide for alcohol use disorder. That made it a covered medicine in every state's Medicaid program, including the nineteen that never took the obesity match, and it gave the quieting effect a clinical name. In May 2034 the FDA approved it for children aged six to eleven, with growth charts every quarter, after some children in the trial grew more slowly during rapid weight loss. About a hundred and fifty thousand children under twelve have started. Half of all American children now live with a parent who is on the drug or cycling off it.

The bones keep breaking. The Medicare analysis this spring put the excess at about eighteen thousand hip fractures a year among long-term older users. Scans run sixteen to twenty-four weeks behind across the Sun Belt. Medicare's rule still demands one every year, and doctors are now allowed to write 'ordered' on the form while their patients wait. Roughly one older ever-user in four is off on a pause or a lapse. The drug is billed to Part D and the hips to Part A.

What moved fastest was taste. Once a twenty-five-dollar pen could make anyone thin, thinness stopped telling anyone anything. In Brooklyn, Austin and Los Angeles the prestige body is built: shoulders, quads, a DEXA printout shown like a credit score. The prestige behaviour is eating. Appetite rooms serve long menus to young people who eat big in public, some on dose-holiday weekends. Dating apps added a 'DEXA verified' badge, and a small scandal followed over people who claimed to be unmedicated and were not. Muscle takes coaching, protein and time. The bottom income third finally reached thin, at 33.5 percent use, and discovered that the look now reads as cheap.

The calm is still for sale, at about six million subscriptions, listed in benefits catalogues beside meditation apps. The first independent study of low-dose users found a small, unclear effect. At top doses it is still about one user in eight. The young subculture that rejects it calls the unblunted state 'colour'. Everyone is waiting for the generic again, now for 2035.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Renée Okafor, thirty-one, takes her pill at 5:40 with water and waits the thirty minutes. Fifty milligrams, Wegovy, $25 copay on the clinic's plan. Her plan gates at the six-month weigh-in. She did hers in March at the kiosk by the blood-pressure cuff and lost 11 percent. Pass.

She is a medical assistant at a pediatric practice in Columbus. At nine a boy named Theo, eight, stands on the scale for his growth check. His mother asks if the shot is why he cried less at the dentist. Renée writes down the height. Point four centimetres since February. She flags it.

At lunch the front desk orders one shared tray of bowls. Danielle, twenty-four, eats two brisket sandwiches at the counter, slowly, so people can see her do it. She is off the drug. She wants everyone to know.

Renée's mother calls from Phoenix. Her DEXA is in nineteen weeks. The doctor wrote 'ordered' on the form. She asks whether that counts. Renée says it counts.

After work Renée goes to the strip-mall gym where the coach squats her and calls her 'under-muscled' in a kind voice. The class costs $140 a month. She is the only one there on the pill, or the only one who says so.

At home her brother Marcus has a capsule bottle on the counter. Shenzhen postmark, $30, no lot number. He says it is for drinking, not weight. She does not ask what dose.

At ten she looks at the app badge, 'DEXA verified', and closes it.
